## Observations

### Shared installer payload sinorag.7z holds sinorag.exe 0.5.0 and is no longer tracked

`verified` · `@sinorag.intake.shared-payload-stale/3` · scope `path "gui-installer/sinorag-installer-pdf-intake/**"`, `path "gui-installer/sinorag-installer-winsafe/**"`, `path "gui-installer/sinorag-installer/sinorag.7z"`

gui-installer/sinorag-installer/sinorag.7z (21,131,926 bytes) unpacks to a sinorag.exe built 2026-05-28 that reports `sinorag 0.5.0`; Cargo.toml is at 0.5.5. That exe has no text_profile support: over indexes built by the document intake (text_profile = "words") the phrases "COOLANT Pump" and "heron colony" return 0 hits and the fragment "pum" returns 1, where a 0.5.5 release build returns 1, 1 and 0. The file is no longer tracked: commit 23e3fd8 removed it from the index and added it to .gitignore (line 11), at the owner's request because it is old; it is still on disk in this checkout. The Freya and winsafe CBETA installers embed this payload and read their expected version from Cargo.toml, so a fresh clone cannot build them until a payload is packed there, and with the stale file they re-extract it on every run. The document intake embeds its own tracked gui-installer/sinorag-installer-pdf-intake/sinorag.7z (0.5.5, packed by make-payload.ps1); its build.rs falls back to the shared file only when that one is missing, and then refuses it for the version mismatch.

### CBETA indexes and tool outputs unchanged by word-layout normalization

`verified` · `@sinorag.evidence.cbeta-regression-word-layout/1`

doc_table.bin, catalog.index, phrase.index and tfidf.index byte-identical (TF-IDF vocab 14767 both); 39/39 tool outputs identical, all ok=true. Working tree was uncommitted on top of HEAD 576bcec.

### English document intake: search, similarity and MCP verified end to end

`verified` · `@sinorag.evidence.english-intake-end-to-end/1`

Search is case-insensitive and whole-word ("COOLANT Pump" hits; "pum" no hits; 3-letter "NEC" works via scan fallback); Chinese search unchanged; similar ranks pump docs with pump docs and heron docs with heron docs on shared words; MCP instructions include the word-corpus section; scanned page OCR'd verbatim; re-runs skip known files by hash. sinorag lib 81 tests, intake 9 tests pass.

### MCP surface and intake refinement: tests, two-client sweep and GUI install/uninstall on the uncommitted tree

`verified` · `@sinorag.evidence.mcp-surface-refinement-run/1` · scope `path "gui-installer/sinorag-installer-pdf-intake/**"`, `path "src/agent/**"`, `path "src/mcp/**"`, `path "src/tools/**"`, `path "tests/mcp_stdio.rs"`

Observed 2026-11-06 on the working tree over ffd166f (changes uncommitted). Root `cargo test`: 95 unit tests and 2 tests in tests/mcp_stdio.rs passed; one earlier full run failed vector_index::tests::build_open_and_search_roundtrip, which passed on 6 reruns and in the next full run, in a module this work did not touch. Intake `cargo test --lib`: 24 passed. Release sinorag-intake.exe installed into a scratch folder with OpenCode and both shortcut boxes unchecked: 6 documents indexed (921 passages, including a 434-page PDF); an empty text file, a PDF named .txt, a ZIP-signature file named .html and 20 KB of an executable named .txt were each reported as failed with the reason and not stored. A second run of a rebuilt installer over an install of the same version logged `Replacing SinoRAG 0.5.5 with this installer's build of it`, added one new document and skipped one already indexed. Against the installed release sinorag.exe: the TypeScript SDK client listed 27 tools (tools/list 38,301 characters, no outputSchema, no write tools) and delivered 10 of 10 calls; a 71-call sweep returned 55 successes and 16 error results, each an intended error case (invalid_args, passage_not_found, readonly_violation, unknown_tool, missing_vector_index), with no internal_error, no non-JSON line on stdout and no server exit. `sinorag agent` with OpenCode missing stayed open when started in its own console and exited at once in a shared one; a dry run kept a `model` key and a second MCP entry in an existing opencode.json. The uninstaller listed two entries it had not created before asking, and after `y` the folder and the HKCU uninstall key were gone. During development a recursion in the related-passages fallback overflowed the stack on a three-word phrase; after the fix the same call and the sweep completed.
